messages.subject: Unexpected modification index value
parts:
Responding to a test question, a student of mine produced  modification index values that are larger than the chi-square for the model. I have understood the modification index as a lower bound on the reduction in chi-square if a constraint is relaxed, which would mean that the modification index cannot be larger than the chi-square. The data are attached as an R binary file. Here is the erroneous syntax:
errmodel<-'
# regression
f5 ~ f3 + f4
f3 ~ f1
f4 ~ f2
# factor/indicator
f1 =~ y1 + y2 + y3
f2 =~ y4 + y5
f3 =~ A*y6 + B*y7 + C*y8 + D*y9
f4 =~ A*y10 + B*y11 + C*y12 + D*y13
f5 =~ y14
# covariance
f1 ~~ f2
f3 ~~ f4
f5 ~~ 0.4*f5'
The "correct" syntax is similar except that the residual variance of y14 is constrained to 0.4, while the residual variance of f5 is free. So just changing "f5" to "y14" here produces the correct syntax.

Then run the model and obtain modification indices:
 errmodel.out <- sem(model=errmodel, data=f18q1data)
summary(errmodel.out)
modindices(errmodel.out,sort = T,minimum.value = 100)

The results include:
  Estimator                                         ML
  Model Fit Test Statistic                     372.285
  Degrees of freedom                                76
  P-value (Chi-square)                           0.000

and:
> modindices(errmodel.out,sort = T,minimum.value = 100)
   lhs op rhs      mi   epc sepc.lv sepc.all sepc.nox
18  f5 =~ y14 376.278 0.507   0.454    0.507    0.507
21  f5 ~~  f5 376.277 0.406   0.499    0.499    0.499
35 y14 ~~ y14 376.277 0.406   0.000    0.000    0.000

I was pleased to see the modification index pointing directly at the error, but I don't think the value should be this high. If I run the "correct" syntax, I get:

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Unexpected modification index value
parts:
On 10/23/18 3:44 PM, Edward Rigdon wrote:
> Responding to a test question, a student of mine produced  modification
> index values that are larger than the chi-square for the model. I have
> understood the modification index as a lower bound on the reduction in
> chi-square if a constraint is relaxed, which would mean that the
> modification index cannot be larger than the chi-square.

Strictly speaking, this is only true asymptotically, because then the
LRT and the score test will agree. The LRT will certainly give you a
chi-square difference lower than the chi-square test statistic, but the
score test may produce larger MI values.

In this particular case, I believe it is (partly) due to numerical
imprecision. The 'score' (the gradient of the objective function) for
the model including the 'relaxed' parameters contains some rather large
values. When squared and multiplied by N, we get (for the first 40-ish
elements):

Browse[2]> zapsmall(N * lavTech(FIT, "gradient.logl")^2 )
[1] 0.0000 0.0000 0.0000 0.0000 0.0000 0.0000 0.0000
0.0000

0.0494

0.0000
[25] 0.0000 0.0000 0.0000 0.0000 0.0000 0.0000 0.0000
0.0000

2.5514
[41] 2.4034 0.6832 0.4259 0.0178 0.0499 0.7416 1.6873
4.2230

Here, the large elements (573.8157, 896.5864) will eventually lead to MI
values larger than the chi-square test statistic.

For what it is worth, Mplus produces very similar values (see below).

Yves.
